correctness.rationale: A direct partial-trace identity proves the complete spectrum from the binary cut rank. A graph automorphism reduces each affine hyperplane to a support-s canonical one; inactive coordinates factor. The two cross-constraint operators have Frobenius-conjugate eigenvalues over F4, hence identical kernels. Counting nonzero F4 tuples with additive sum one yields (3^(s-1)-(-1)^(s-1))/4 zero characters and the displayed rank, with no excluded dimensions. Extremal support sizes follow from the exact alternating rank fraction. Independent explicit adjacency row reductions cover 1113 affine instances and direct state partial traces cover dimensions 1 and 2; finite experiments are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Codimension-one affine cuts are a canonical, symmetry-controlled family in ternary Hamming networks; the complete spectrum and sharp all-cut extremizers are natural exact invariants, not arbitrary finite slices. A dimension-independent 2/3 minimal entanglement fraction at two-coordinate normals, maximal entanglement at one-coordinate normals and an alternating approach to a 3/4 fraction are mathematically structural and not a mere restatement of the generic cut-rank rule. Full-spectrum finite-system benchmarks have a plausible use without requiring speculative experimental claims.
